_comment: Hand-edited policy for the reference archive tool. Generated state lives in
the archive manifest, never here, so a re-run never conflicts with a human
decision. A fork changes 'depth' and re-renders offline.
This repository is the 'Top 10 Web Hacking Techniques' reading list. Each
year is its own Markdown list (2006.md .. 2025.md), and the archive is
organised the same way: a reference is filed under the year list that cites
it, in archived-references/md/<year>/ with its PDF in
archived-references/pdf/<year>/. See tools/references/refslib/collections.py.
The two format trees under archive_dir, split so the binary PDFs stay
out of the Markdown tree: archived-references/md/<year>/<slug>.md and
archived-references/pdf/<year>/<slug>.pdf. The reports about the archive
(README.md, needs-work.md, excluded.md, store-gaps.md, manifest.json,
history.jsonl)
live at the archive_dir root, beside both trees.
The archive is grouped by the year LIST that cites a reference, derived
from the citing file name (2016-17.md -> 2016-17). A reference cited by
more than one year is filed under the first citation. Anything cited only
outside a year list falls back to 'misc'.
Tracked YYYY-ai.md files are detected automatically. Only citations
between these exact markers are harvested; scoring, watchlists and
dropped candidates remain source notes rather than archive records.
Tracked paths whose URLs are NOT resources the year lists point at.
This is a path prefix list, not an exclusion RULE: nothing here is a
judgement about a URL, only about which files carry the reading list.
README.md is navigation: it links to each year list and to the original
nomination/results pages, which are the index rather than the techniques.
archived-references/ is the archive's OWN OUTPUT; harvesting it would treat
every link inside an archived article as a citation of ours, which is how a
few hundred references silently become thousands. references-md/ is that
output tree's PREVIOUS name, kept as a guard so a stale checkout of it is
never harvested. tools/ and .claude/ are this repository's own tooling,
not sources the lists cite.
Store binaries here. Many entries on these lists are PDFs, slide decks or
conference papers, and the whole point of the archive is that a technique
survives its source going offline - so the PDF/paper IS downloaded and
converted to Markdown like any other document.
Video is the one kind still not mirrored: the useful part of a talk is its
metadata, description and captions (see the 'transcripts' command), not the
media file. Images are read at their own URL, not mirrored (link-only).
EXECUTABLES AND ARCHIVES ARE NEVER DOWNLOADED, and that is not a setting:
the list lives in refslib/kinds.py (EXECUTABLE_SUFFIXES) and acquisition
refuses the kind before any route runs. A program is not a document - the
technique lives in the write-up - so fetching one gains nothing and puts an
executable on the maintainer's disk and in the content store. It covers
every OS, formats that only look harmless (.chm is a compiled, scriptable
Windows binary), and archives, whose contents are unknown until unpacked.
The 'pdf' command makes a PDF copy of each archived Markdown file, so a
reference can be read or shared as a self-contained document. It renders
OUR archived Markdown (offline, no third-party page scripts) to HTML and
prints it with headless Chromium in the locked-down Docker toolbox.
No host browser is discovered or used, and the print container has no network.
PDFs go in the layout.pdf_tree tree, parallel to the Markdown tree.
skip_kinds: kinds never turned into a PDF. A talk is a video, not a page,
and a source that is ALREADY a PDF is copied rather than re-rendered.

ledger._comment: Optional and read-only. No curation ledger exists for this repo, so every URL is probed. Left here so a future ledger can be pointed at without a schema change.

_comment: Only genuine host RENAMES belong here, as "old.example": "new.example".
Two hosts publishing the same article are a content-dedup question, not a
URL identity one. Empty because no host cited by these year lists has been
renamed; add an entry when one is, so both spellings resolve to one entry.

_locale_stripped_hosts_comment: Hosts that serve one document under a locale prefix (/en-us/, /fr-fr/) where
the prefix is not part of its identity. A flat list of host names - it is
read straight into a set, so nothing but hostnames may go in it. Empty
because no host cited by these year lists does this.
